questions.text: An angle \(\theta\) satisfies \(\sin\theta+\cos\theta=\frac13\), and \(\theta\) lies in Quadrant II. Find the exact value of \(\tan\theta\).

Without using a calculator, determine the sign and exact value of  
\[
\sec\!\left(-\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)+\csc\!\left(\frac{11\pi}{6}\right).
\]

A point \(P(x,y)\) lies on the terminal side of an angle \(\theta\) in Quadrant III, and
\[
x+y=-7,\qquad \frac{x}{y}=\cot\theta=\frac34.
\]
Find the exact values of \(\sin\theta,\cos\theta,\tan\theta\).
Two sides of a triangle have lengths \(13\) and \(20\), and the included angle is \(150^\circ\). Find the area of the triangle.

An observer is \(5280\) ft from the launch pad of a rocket. At one moment the angle of elevation is \(45^\circ\); one minute later it is \(60^\circ\). Assuming the rocket rises straight up at constant speed during that minute, how many feet does it rise?

questions.text: Two triangles have the same area. The first triangle has side lengths of $5$ and $8$ with an included angle of $15^\circ$. The second triangle has side lengths of $4$ and $10$ with an included obtuse angle $\theta$. What is the degree measure of $\theta$?

questions.text: Given that $\sin \theta + \cos \theta = \frac{1}{5}$ and that $\theta$ lies in Quadrant II, determine the exact value of $\sin \theta - \cos \theta$.

questions.text:
The six vertices of a regular hexagon centered at the origin correspond to standard position angles $\theta_1, \theta_2, \dots, \theta_6$. If one of the vertices lies on the positive $x$-axis, mentally evaluate the product:
$(1 - \sin \theta_1)(1 - \sin \theta_2)(1 - \sin \theta_3)(1 - \sin \theta_4)(1 - \sin \theta_5)(1 - \sin \theta_6)$

questions.text: A circular sector has an acute central angle $\theta$. The ratio of the area of the triangle formed by its two bounding radii and the chord connecting their endpoints, to the area of the entire sector, is exactly $\frac{3}{\pi}$. Find the degree measure of $\theta$.
